props.title: Sleeping with Other People

sections.content: **Sleeping with Other People (2015)** (2015) brilliantly modernizes the When Harry Met Sally formula for the hookup era. Writer-director Leslye Headland crafts a raw, honest rom-com about two serial cheaters (Jason Sudeikis and Alison Brie) who lost their virginity to each other in college, reconnect years later, and try to maintain a platonic friendship despite their obvious chemistry. Like **Trainwreck** (2015) and **Friends with Benefits** (2011), it subverts romantic comedy tropes while still delivering the emotional payoff fans crave.

sections.content: What sets **Sleeping with Other People** apart is its brutally honest exploration of modern dating anxieties. While films like **500 Days of Summer** (2009) examined relationship dysfunction through a male lens, Headland's script gives equal weight to both leads' emotional damage. The film's frank discussions of sex, intimacy issues, and self-sabotage feel more aligned with contemporary shows like **You're the Worst** (2014-2019) than traditional rom-coms.

The film also excels at building authentic friendship chemistry before romantic tension. Like **Plus One** (2019) and **Set It Up** (2018), it understands that modern romance often blooms from genuine connection rather than meet-cute contrivance. Sudeikis and Brie's easy rapport recalls the winning dynamics of **What If** (2013) and **The F Word** (2013). SUBHEAD: Modern Rom-Com Evolution

sections.content: **Sleeping with Other People** represents a key evolution in romantic comedies, joining films like **The Big Sick** (2017) and **Long Shot** (2019) in prioritizing character development and contemporary social dynamics over formulaic plotting. Its treatment of sexuality and emotional intimacy feels particularly relevant in an era of dating apps and shifting relationship norms.
